decision.verdict: KEEP — documented-unstable, structurally proven, formally outside the 1.0 bit-freeze
rationale: the fast lane's only promise is STRUCTURAL and it is machine-checked for any surprisal function (LEAN T2/S5/S6): tiling, round-trip, and intern ids can never break — what is unstable is which patches the approximation draws
the measured surprisal deviation is 1.19e-07 (bound 5e-07 asserted in research/fastlane_parity.json) and segmentation on the shipped domains is IDENTICAL

the measured speed delta is +4.0% at best on this host-day — marginal, but the lane costs nothing to keep (one flag through the judge), the FST-lane experiments (v0.9.0b) showed the approximation is not a big win even when it works, and removing a documented API in a hardening release is an unnecessary break
if a future release ever fails its own parity bound (5e-07), the decision flips to REMOVE — the record re-measures on every parity run
decision.contract_note: 1.0 bit-freeze covers the exact lane only; the fast lane stays documented-unstable by this decision (PLAN_v0.9 frozen contract).
